clue.text: Trouble leads to restriction on worship

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, a kind of trouble
a ration is a fixed limit on what may be had, a restriction

explanation.surface: Problems arise when religious practice is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is devoted reverence, the act of worship itself.

clue.text: Mother has to request material

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of animals
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Mum must ask for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric.

clue.text: Wound up the worse for drink

explanation.surface: Someone ended the evening tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A line wound in on a spool has been reeled in; someone drunk staggers, i.e. reeled.

clue.text: Unexpected developments from Women's Institute in the back-streets

indicators.note: the Institute's letters go inside the streets
back means the street letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, so streets gives two of them
WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: Plot turns emerge from a women's group meeting in the back alleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Twists are sudden changes of direction in a plot.

clue.text: Violent crime generates public fury

explanation.surface: Brutal offences spark popular anger.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocious act is an outrage, and so is the indignation it provokes.

clue.text: Manufacture underwear as a temporary measure

parts.note: to make is to manufacture
a shift is a woman's simple undergarment, a chemise

explanation.surface: Run up some undergarments as a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift is a stopgap substitute used for the time being.

clue.text: Acknowledge someone, if you know him

explanation.surface: Greet a person you are acquainted with.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is true is to admit it; and you identify a person on sight when you know them.

clue.text: Criminal road-speed amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters the text, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: A change to the speed limit is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' could be an adjective about the amendment; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw.

clue.text: A sprinter's challenge proves a bit of a bloomer

explanation.surface: A runner's dare to a rival turns out to be something of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant; read as two words the answer is the runner's taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner daring a rival says 'try to beat me in a race'; botanically the word names a flower cluster on a stalk, part of a flowering plant.

clue.text: I am to settle the dispute without delay

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'm
to mediate is to intervene to settle a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to resolve a quarrel straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at once, with no pause, is instant.

clue.text: Make good one's losses after a military putsch

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler hopes to win back what was lost after an army takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-COUP: a coup again, the one that follows an earlier putsch.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover what was lost is to recoup it; a second seizure of power after a putsch is a further coup.

clue.text: Fresh ale is sent as required

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Newly brewed beer is shipped out because customers demand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like praise for the beer but signals that ALE IS SENT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, needed without fail.

clue.text: A black eye for the bootblack

explanation.surface: The shoe-polisher ended up with a bruised face.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised eye is slang a shiner; a bootblack is someone who polishes shoes until they gleam.

clue.text: The crusaders' zeal in military action

parts.note: crusaders fought under the emblem of the cross, so the cross is theirs
fire is ardour or zeal

explanation.surface: Religious warriors show fervour in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Intersecting gunfire from two or more positions is a feature of battle.

clue.text: No amity is developed!

indicators.note: developed means grown into something different, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Friendship has failed to form.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is hostility, the absence of friendliness.

clue.text: Just a trifle game

explanation.surface: Only a small matter of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is something unimportant, and also a board game where balls are struck into holes.

clue.text: Main ingredient cheese and onion pie

indicators.note: an ingredient is something contained within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: The chief component of a savoury pastry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but in crosswords 'the main' is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean.

clue.text: Heavens above!

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise, read literally as the heavens overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The firmament overhead is called the heavens.

clue.text: In action the soldier has it to hand

definitions.text: In action the soldier has it to hand

parts.words: In action the soldier has it to hand
parts.note: a fighting man keeps his weapon at the ready, and the limb also ends in a hand

explanation.surface: A fighting man keeps something close by in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon is an arm, and the upper limb has a hand at its end.

clue.text: Make a thorough search for smuggled sherry

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran means smuggled
sack is an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: Customs officers comb everything looking for contraband fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to go through a place exhaustively, often roughly.

clue.text: The umpire exercised his right to say no

definitions.text: The umpire exercised his right to say no

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is an umpire
a right exercised is a right used

explanation.surface: An official declined a request.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to something is declining it.

clue.text: Vegetable which upsets one's little Mary

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets would overturn; here it signals reading the name from the end back

parts.note: May is a pet form of the name Mary

explanation.surface: A vegetable that gives someone an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is old British slang for the stomach, which makes the surface about indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy tuber is a staple root vegetable.

clue.text: A lot of trouble for the maid

parts.note: a big amount is a lot
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: The servant causes much grief.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, from a waiting-woman in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: An abigail is a lady's personal servant.

clue.text: Craft shown by a politician in isolation sick-bay

indicators.note: the politician is placed inside the sick-bay

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is a school sick-bay where patients are isolated
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A boat is displayed by an MP who is quarantined in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed Chinese boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Able to pay fifty-one pounds

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone can settle a bill of fifty-one pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid in finance means having cash readily available, solvent.

clue.text: Empty one container into another

indicators.note: the first container goes inside the second

parts.note: a vat is another container
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Pour the contents of one vessel into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied, with nothing in it.

clue.text: His five-year plan was a quick way to a nil return

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: return means the word nil comes back, read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader's economic programme quickly led to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soviet leader launched the Five-Year Plans for the USSR economy from 1928.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph, the Soviet dictator, introduced the first five-year plan for industrialisation.

clue.text: Leaving it to be resolved by self-appointed policeman

indicators.note: resolved here means broken up and reworked, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a problem for an unofficial enforcer to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be resolved' reads as settling a matter but signals reworking LEAVING IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes the law into their own hands without authority.

clue.text: Did he angle for an Anglican archiepiscopacy?

definitions.text: Did he angle for an Anglican archiepiscopacy?

parts.words: Did he angle for an Anglican archiepiscopacy?
parts.note: to angle is to try to catch fish with rod and line; the same surname was borne by Geoffrey, Archbishop of Canterbury 1945-61

explanation.surface: Did a churchman scheme to become an archbishop?
explanation.definitionFit: One who angles catches fish, and Geoffrey of that surname held the see of Canterbury from 1945 to 1961.

clue.text: King Cole leads a fashionable mass meeting, of course

parts.note: Nat King Cole was the American singer, so King Cole gives Nat
U stands for upper-class, hence smart or fashionable
a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: A famous singer heads a trendy big gathering, as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course and naturally both mean as might be expected.

clue.text: Maraca for a well-known conductor

explanation.surface: A percussion instrument is linked to a famous maestro.
explanation.definitionFit: A maraca is a shaken percussion instrument, a kind of baby's toy noise-maker too; Sir Simon of that surname is a celebrated English orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Grand Old Man pleased with a piece of jewellery

parts.note: glad means pleased
a stone is a gem, a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: An elder statesman is delighted with a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Old Man' (G.O.M.) was the nickname of William Gladstone, the Victorian Liberal prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian prime minister William Ewart was nicknamed the G.O.M. by admirers.
